purpose: Refactor the monolithic 568-line app/src/index.ts into focused single-responsibility subscriber modules with shared utilities, reducing the entry point to ~42 lines.
riskRationale: All 12 previously reported code-quality issues from the initial review have been fixed. Two new critical bugs were introduced in the process: (1) the audit subscriber passes AbortSignal as a directory-path argument to handleAudit(), and (2) the fix subscriber reads labels from the wrong payload field. Both are one-line fixes with no breaking changes.

text: The refactoring is well-structured with clean separation of concerns, proper dependency injection, consistent error handling, and JSDoc on all public APIs. All 12 previously reported issues are correctly resolved. Two critical bugs remain: the audit subscriber passes AbortSignal in the wrong positional argument slot, and the fix subscriber reads labels from the top-level payload instead of the issue object for issue.labeled events.

reasoning: Two critical bugs block merge: (1) audit.ts:20 passes AbortSignal as 4th argument (targetDir) instead of 7th argument (signal) to handleAudit(), breaking cancellation; (2) fix.ts:18 reads labels from fixPayload.labels instead of fixIssue.labels, breaking autofix-trigger for issue.labeled events.

message: Entry point reduced from 568 to ~42 lines — only validates env, creates services, registers subscribers, attaches webhook handler, and handles SIGTERM cleanup. Clear orchestration role.
Clean central router that composes all subscriber factories and lib-based subscribers in a single registration call with dependency injection.
Feature-enabled guard moved before mention parsing, avoiding unnecessary work when conversation feature is disabled.
Dead pull_request?.before fallback removed — previousHeadSha now reads only from the root-level webhook 'before' field.
AbortSignal consistently propagated to handleCommand(), matching the pattern used across other subscribers.
Unused _parentId variable removed, and unused null guard on required LearningStore parameter in discover.ts removed.
Replaced dynamic import() with a static import, enabling better bundler and tree-shaking support.

AbortSignal passed as the 4th positional argument (targetDir?: string) to handleAudit() instead of the 7th argument (signal?). handleAudit() signature expects (repo, token, config, targetDir?, promptName?, tempDir?, signal?). This means the AbortSignal object is misinterpreted as a directory path, causing a TypeScript type error (TS2345) and silently breaking cancellation support.
suggestion: Pass the signal as the 7th positional argument with explicit undefined placeholders for the intermediate optional parameters: await handleAudit(event.repo || '', getToken(), config, undefined, undefined, undefined, signal);
suggestionCode: await handleAudit(event.repo || '', getToken(), config, undefined, undefined, undefined, signal);

message: Labels are read from fixPayload.labels (top-level payload) instead of fixIssue.labels (inside the issue object). GitHub's issues.labeled webhook payload has no top-level labels field — labels live at payload.issue.labels. This makes the autofix-trigger label detection for issue.labeled events always fail. All existing references in auto-analyze.ts (line 27) and question-answered.ts (line 22) correctly read from issue.labels.
suggestion: Change fixLabels to read from fixIssue.labels (inside the issue object) instead of fixPayload.labels (top-level), matching the pattern used in auto-analyze.ts:27.
suggestionCode: const fixLabels = fixIssue?.labels as Array<Record<string, string>> | undefined;
